steps.title: Keep the intended field focused for Stop
steps.body: Place the cursor in a writable field. Keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop. Mumble then uses the field focused at Stop instead of asking you to move into a separate editor.
steps.proof: The destination is frozen when Stop is requested—not when recording starts.

steps.title: Start with the deliberate global Dictate command
steps.body: Invoke Dictate from the application you are already using. The Island shows Listening, then Transcribing, so recording and processing are visible rather than implied.
steps.proof: The same global command starts and stops the dictation.

steps.title: Transcribe on this computer by default
steps.body: Local transcription is the default. Recorded audio stays on this computer unless the user explicitly selects Cloud transcription.
steps.proof: Optional shaping is a separate finished-text decision.

steps.title: Return once, or recover safely
steps.body: Mumble attempts to insert the finished text at the field frozen when Stop was requested. If insertion cannot complete, the result is saved in the Deck and History for Copy or Paste latest instead of being sent again automatically.
steps.proof: Later focus changes do not authorize a new destination or a second blind insertion.

tasks.title: Everyday notes

Use the global Dictate command and speak the thought in ordinary language.

Continue from the inserted text, or use the saved Deck result if delivery could not complete.

tasks.title: Longer text
tasks.summary: Draft a connected passage without replacing the document you already chose.
steps: Place the cursor in the draft where the next passage belongs.
Start Dictate and speak the passage at a comfortable pace.
Keep or return focus to that field before you choose Stop; the Island then shows the transition into transcription.
Review the returned text in the draft, or recover the finished result from the Deck if insertion was blocked.

tasks.title: Across applications
tasks.summary: Carry the same Write sequence into another writable desktop application.
steps: Open the destination application and place its cursor in the intended field.
Invoke the global Dictate command without leaving that application.
Speak, then keep or return focus to the intended field before you choose Stop.
Mumble attempts one return to the field frozen at Stop; if that field is unavailable at delivery, it keeps the text in the Deck rather than inserting elsewhere.

steps.title: Choose the selected microphone or supported audio

steps.proof: Direct video import and computer-audio capture are not current input choices.

steps.title: Keep a private local recording
steps.body: Mumble writes microphone capture to a private local WAV while the meeting is running. Stop & save finishes that durable recording before transcription starts; imported audio is normalised into the same private meeting library first.
steps.proof: A failed or interrupted transcription does not silently discard a recording that was saved successfully.

steps.title: Choose Local or Cloud transcription explicitly
steps.body: Local transcription is the default and keeps meeting audio on this computer. Cloud transcription sends meeting audio to the deliberately selected configured provider after the route choice; the saved private local recording remains the working source.
steps.proof: The current effective route is shown before, during, and after capture.

steps.title: Search, replay, and review the record
steps.body: Search titles and full transcripts in the local meeting library, find matching transcript segments, and play the original recording in the computer's audio player. Best-effort speaker grouping can help review, but labels may need correction and can be less reliable for long or Cloud recordings.
steps.proof: Transcript search and playback are review tools; the screenshot data is a labelled demonstration.

steps.title: Export first; choose analysis separately
steps.body: Export a ready record as TXT, Markdown, JSON, HTML, or the clipboard. Summary, action-item, decision, and question tools remain optional and run only when a configured analysis route is available and you choose the action. The original recording is never sent for analysis.
steps.proof: Hosted analysis receives transcript text only; it is separate from the transcription route.

tasks.title: Meeting

Choose Stop & save. Mumble finishes the private local recording before transcription begins.
Search the saved meeting, review or replay it, export the ready transcript, and choose optional analysis only when its route is available.

tasks.title: Lecture

steps: Select the room microphone in Mumble and check the effective transcription route before the lecture begins.
Record the lecture, pausing and resuming around breaks; current source limits one recording or import to four hours.
Stop & save so the private recording is durable before Mumble transcribes it through the selected route.
Search the transcript for a topic, replay the original recording in the computer's player, and export the ready record for your notes.

tasks.title: Existing recording

Mumble normalises and saves a private local copy before background transcription begins.
The selected Local route keeps audio here; an explicit Cloud route sends audio to the configured transcription provider.
Search the completed transcript, play the saved recording, export the record, or choose optional transcript-only analysis when available.

mechanism.title: Shape routes finished text with the choice frozen.
mechanism.summary: The mode, selected material, provider route, model, and privacy boundary are captured for one shaping action. A hosted route cannot silently become another provider or take the recorded audio with it.

steps.title: Keep Text useful without AI
steps.body: Text is the everyday default: deterministic local cleanup produces punctuated text without an account or provider key. Foreign is a separate opt-in local term-assistance mode that prioritises the languages chosen in Settings rather than translating the whole result.
steps.proof: Local dictation remains useful with no Mumble account, provider key, or paid service.

steps.title: Choose Prompt, Email, or Reply deliberately
steps.body: Prompt asks for a structured role, task, constraints, and output. Email requests a greeting, body, sign-off, and an optional subject. Reply uses selected context to draft a direct response. Each is a real shaping form, not a generic chat assistant.
steps.proof: Text, Prompt, Email, Reply, and Foreign remain distinct modes.

steps.title: Apply a preset or custom shaping instruction
steps.body: The Deck offers 20 built-in presets for actions such as Improve, Make shorter, Deep Thinking, Summarise, and Extract facts, plus five custom shaping slots the user can define. A chosen mode can also control the final form.
steps.proof: Analysis is a chosen preset action over selected material—not an automatic claim about every dictation.

steps.title: Freeze the effective configured route
steps.body: Cerebras and OpenRouter are the current supported hosted text choices in Settings. A user-supplied key and a confirmed model are required before the hosted route is ready. External providers may charge under their own terms.
steps.proof: Hosted shaping sends finished text—not recorded audio—and cannot swap to another provider silently.

steps.title: Treat local shaping as configuration-dependent
steps.body: A compatible local model can be used only when the user separately supplies and enables it. No local model is bundled or adopted, so the website does not present local Prompt, Email, or Reply shaping as an out-of-box result.
steps.proof: Device-only remains a fail-closed privacy choice when hosted processing is unavailable or disabled.

steps.title: Review the saved result
steps.body: A completed Deck shaping job is saved before Mumble attempts the selected field. The visitor examples describe the sequence and form only; they do not promise a provider’s exact output, quality, or speed.
steps.proof: Illustrative text is labelled wherever it is not a genuine product capture.

steps.title: Add a supported document

steps.title: Choose an optional summary separately
steps.body: Summary is not part of playback. When you choose it and a configured analysis route is ready, Mumble sends document text to that provider; the resulting summary can then be read through the separately configured speech route.
steps.proof: A summary action and text-to-speech playback are two distinct online decisions.

steps.title: Search the Deck history
steps.body: The Deck keeps transcripts, clipboard captures, prompts, emails, and finished results available together. Search all Deck content or narrow the view by content type, then filter to Starred material when you want the items deliberately kept for reuse.
steps.proof: Clipboard capture and saved Deck material remain local in the current product path.

steps.title: Reuse the material you found
steps.body: Open a matching Deck row, read it in full, copy or paste the latest item, or select saved text for a deliberate shaping action. Starred copies survive ordinary source-history clearing within the product's bounded favourites store.
steps.proof: Deck actions work on saved Mumble material; they do not become app-and-file search.

steps.title: Open Mumble Find for this computer
steps.body: Mumble Find is a separate, keyboard-first local launcher for installed apps and indexed files. Type a query, move through local results, then choose Open, Show in folder, or Drag to another app where the result supports that action.
steps.proof: Hosted web results never enter the Mumble Find list.

steps.title: Choose Web Search only when you mean to go online

steps.proof: The provider and selected-text boundary are frozen for one short-lived confirmation.

steps.title: Keep failure truthful
steps.body: Mumble reports Web Search opened only after the browser opener confirms success. If the browser could not open, the request reports that failure and tells the user to check the default browser before trying again.
steps.proof: A consumed consent request cannot silently become a success message or open twice.

steps: Invoke the separate Mumble Find command; the centred launcher identifies itself as Private on this device.
Type the app or filename. The list contains local results only and never inserts hosted web results.
Move through the results with the keyboard and confirm the illustrated result is the local item you intended.
Choose Open, Show in folder, or Drag to another app when that result offers the action.

example.quote: Compare the project brief with the launch notes.
example.detail: Chosen provider in this demonstration: Perplexity

steps: Select the Deck text you intend to send, then choose the separate Search the web action.
Read the confirmation: it names the chosen provider—Google, Perplexity, or Brave—and shows the selected words.
Choose Keep private to cancel, or choose Search online to send only those selected words to the named provider.
Treat the result literally: Web Search opened appears only after browser success; browser could not open remains a failure with recovery guidance.
